plan.notes: Source: official Washington State University Faculty Senate document 'Spring 2026 UPMCB Bulletin No. 7' (https://facsen.wsu.edu/documents/2026/02/592b-upmcb-7-requirements-updated.pdf), item 'Revise requirements for BS in Computer Science', header '8-26 Computer Science (120 Credits)'. Effective August 2026 (the 2026-2027 catalog year). The bulletin states the requirements 'reflect the undergraduate major curricular changes approved by the Catalog Subcommittee' — i.e., exactly what catalog.wsu.edu publishes for the Pullman BS in Computer Science (School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science). Hand-transcribed 2026-09-30 from the official PDF. Note: catalog.wsu.edu program pages could not be loaded directly (egress timeout on the /Pullman/ path); the Faculty Senate bulletin is the authoritative source of the same approved requirements. Program: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, WSU Pullman; 120 credits minimum. Credit-range caveat: the bulletin shows term totals of 120-122 because 'MATH 220 or 225' is 2 or 3 credits and 'MATH 273 or 301' is 2 or 3 credits. This plan uses the minimum-credit options (MATH 220 = 2 cr, MATH 273 = 2 cr) so the plan sums to exactly 120 = total_credits; choosing MATH 225 (3 cr) and/or MATH 301 (3 cr) raises a student's total to 121-122. Bulletin footnotes transcribed: (1) Two programming paths — C/C++ (CPT S 121, 122, 223, 360) or Java (CPT S 131, 132, 233, 370); students stay on one path. (2) Lab science: one [BSCI] and one [PSCI] course with lab; options include CHEM 105/106, PHYSICS 201+211, PHYSICS 202+212, BIOLOGY 106/107. (3) CPT S Technical Electives: 4 courses (12 cr); at least one course from the Software area and at least one from the Data & Information Management area. (4) UCORE Inquiry: 4 courses (12 cr), one each from four of the five designations ARTS / DIVR / EQJS / HUM / SSCI. (5) Computer Science Electives: 5 courses (15 cr); at least 9 credits must be CPT S courses. UCORE designations in the bulletin: ENGLISH 101 [WRTG], MATH 171 [QUAN], HISTORY 105 [ROOT], CPT S 322 [M], CPT S 423 [CAPS] [M], ENGLISH 402 [WRTG]; lab sciences [BSCI]/[PSCI]. Prerequisites: the bulletin is a term-by-term schedule and does not list course prerequisites, so all prereq arrays are empty; the term sequence itself encodes the recommended order. Milestones: 'Complete Writing Portfolio' (end of Year 2) and 'Complete CPT S Exit Interview and Survey' (final term) are official degree requirements, included as 0-credit completable items. Course titles verified against official WSU sources (tricities.wsu.edu, eecs.wsu.edu, mme.wsu.edu, cyser.wsu.edu, facsen.wsu.edu, registrar.wsu.edu, ceshs.wsu.edu, ecs.vancouver.wsu.edu). Four titles rest on strong corroborated evidence rather than a wsu.edu page and are flagged honestly: CPT S 101 'Introduction to Electrical Engineering and Computer Science' (WSU student transcript + Fall 2025 WSU course repo + Uloop WSU course-notes page, all consistent); CPT S 370 'Systems Programming Java' (consistent with the bulletin's Java-path structure and course listings); ENGLISH 101 'Introductory College Writing' (Uloop WSU course-notes page; WSU Writing program describes it as the introductory college-level academic writing course); MATH 301 'Introduction to Mathematical Reasoning' (Uloop WSU course-notes page; WSU Vancouver plan abbreviates it 'Intro to Math. Reasoning').
